 IND vs NZ, 3rd T20I: India beat New Zealand by 6 wickets, seal series 3-0 after Abhishek Sharma's ton 
 LIVE NOW Share Comments IND vs NZ, 3rd T20I: India beat New Zealand by 6 wickets, seal series 3-0 after Abhishek Sharma's ton
 THE TIMES OF INDIA | Oct 27, 2026, 15:57:01 IST SUMMARY Abhishek Sharma smashed a 38-ball 113 as India beat New Zealand by six wickets to win the third T20 here on Tuesday, giving the visitors an unassailable 3-0 lead in the five-match series. 
 Abhishek and Vaibhav Sooryavanshi (45 off 19) made mincemeat of New Zealand’s bowling attack, hammering 133 for the first wicket in 7.1 overs. India chased down 199 in just 13.2 overs. 
 New Zealand had made 198 for three after being put in to bat for the third game in a row. 
 Daryl Mitchell top scored for the hosts with an unbeaten 89. 
 Brief scores: New Zealand 198/3 in 20 overs (Daryl Mitchell 89 not out, Finn Allen 40; Arshdeep Singh 1/33, Axar Patel 1/36) lost to India 199/4 in 13.2 overs (Vaibhav Sooryavanshi 45, Abhishek Sharma 113; Kyle Jamieson 2/45) by six wickets. Commentary 
 Scorecard 
 15:57 (IST) Oct 27 Still a lot to play for - The T20I series between New Zealand and India might be done in terms of who takes the trophy home, but with the ODI series up next, the remaining two T20I games might serve as a momentum carrier. The hosts will be desperate for a win, whereas India will be brimming with confidence. The 4th T20I is set to be played at Eden Park in Auckland on Friday, October 30. The game is scheduled to begin at 7 am GMT (12.30 pm IST), but be sure to join us a lot sooner for the build-up to the contest as well. Until then, tale care and goodbye.
 15:53 (IST) Oct 27 The Indian skipper - Shreyas Iyer says it was absolutely pleasing to watch Abhishek and Sooryavanshi bat at the top. He admits that when he and Samson were at the crease, the ball was still swinging a bit, and says it was insane how the openers managed to hit it out of the park. He says scoring 100 in five overs is something he has not seen before at the international level. On the message to play fearlessly, Iyer says it is essential, especially overseas where players will be challenged. He credits the openers for an exceptional effort and hopes they continue in the same form with two games remaining. He is glad with how the squad turned up despite the travel and jet lag, calling it mind-boggling. On the bowling, Iyer admits that India were conceding runs when bowling hard lengths or full deliveries, so he asked the bowlers to target the yorkers. That, he details, helped keep New Zealand under ten runs an over, with the plan being to restrict them below 200.
 15:52 (IST) Oct 27 The captain of New Zealand - Mitchell Santner says that it was a tough loss, and it's difficult to stop some of the Indian batters when they get going. He adds that they lost the toss again, but Daryl Mitchell and Bevon Jacobs did well and seemed on course for 200, which didn't quite happen. He also feels that there was some dew, but credits the Indian batters for the way they played. Santner feels that the batting is coming along well, with different guys putting their hands up in different games. On holding himself back during the chase, Santner feels that he saw how Axar Patel went about it in the first innings, and he didn't come on as there were two left-handers going pretty strong, and they will look to find a way during such situations in the future.

 15:47 (IST) Oct 27 Player of Match - No prizes for guessing, and it is Abhishek Sharma who gets the accolade for his swashbuckling knock of 113 off 38 balls. Sharma says the key was simple, saying that he and Vaibhav simply wanted to enjoy themselves, especially in the Powerplay. He explains that while fielding, they absorbed the pressure and noted the extra bounce, but felt the ground dimensions allowed them to make use of the Powerplay and the pace on offer. He praises Vaibhav's start in the first over as really special and says their plan was to build momentum for the team and keep going. On the freedom given by the coaching staff and captain, Abhishek says it is not exactly easy, but preparation behind the scenes makes the difference. He gives a special mention to the coaches and the sidearm throwdowns, saying preparation is crucial for a batter. He adds that reading the conditions, ground dimensions and bowlers helps him choose his shots, and that a good practice session the previous day allowed him to carry that confidence into the match. He feels he had visualised the setting, and it played out that way. Responding to Yuvraj Singh's social media remark that he still cannot score a fifty off 12 balls, Abhishek says he does not know what kind of cricket Yuvraj was playing in that era, but admits that it is not easy at all. He adds that any batter would want to bat like that, but a fifty in 12 balls happens only once in a while. He stresses that he does not chase milestones, and the aim is always to win the game for the team. He says he and Vaibhav wanted to carry that approach through the series, and it worked well.
 15:47 (IST) Oct 27 Presentation time...
 15:46 (IST) Oct 27 Recapping the first innings - Earlier in the game, Shreyas Iyer won yet another toss and asked New Zealand to bat first. Tim Seifert got out pretty early on, but Finn Allen and Daryl Mitchell launched a counter-attack and got the hosts into a position of promise. Allen got out in the 40s, but Mitchell went on to stay on till the end, remaining unbeaten on 89 as Bevon Jacobs played a handy knock as well. India weren't at their best with the ball and Bhuvneshwar Kumar struggled to make an impact yet again, but the death bowling was pretty solid as Prince Yadav made a fine comeback and Arshdeep Singh and Nitish Kumar Reddy nailed their yorkers as well, managing to keep New Zealand under the 200-run mark.

 15:43 (IST) Oct 27 No show in the Powerplay - It was really an underwhelming showing with the ball from the Kiwis in the first 6 overs. Also, Mitchell Santner's reluctance to bowl himself against the two left-handed openers didn't help, and by the time he came on to bowl, the game was long gone. New Zealand conceded 118 runs in the Powerplay, and a total of 178 runs in the first 10 overs, before Kyle Jamieson and Mitchell Santner picked up a few late wickets. Matthew Fisher also got his maiden T20I wicket by dismissing Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, but overall, it was another un-Kiwi like showing in the field from New Zealand.
 15:41 (IST) Oct 27 New opening pair blitz - India made a change up top and sent Vaibhav Sooryavanshi to open alongside Abhishek Sharma, and the duo put on a batting show of the highest order. They racked up 118 runs in the Powerplay, which is a record for a full-member nation in T20Is, before their stand eventually ended at 133 runs. Abhishek, in particular, was on a different tangent as he smoked the ball to all parts of the ground. Sooryavanshi missed out on a half-century, but Sharma notched up a sensational ton off just 35 balls before getting out. India did lose steam towards the end, but managed to get over the line with plenty of time to spare.
 15:39 (IST) Oct 27 Sealing the series in style - India have clinched this five-match T20I series 3-0 with two games in hand, and the third game has been completely one-sided, or at least the second half of the game was. New Zealand have a lot of work to do now if they want to avoid a clean sweep.
 15:38 (IST) Oct 27 India vs New Zealand Live Score : 199/4 (13.2 overs) 4 Overs 13.2 Score 199 - 4 Kyle Jamieson to Naman Dhir, FOUR! An anticlimactic end to the match, but India beat New Zealand by 6 wickets and 40 balls to spare. A good-length delivery bashed hard into the pitch by Jamieson. Naman Dhir waits back and looks to punch it to the off side, but the ball straightens up a bit, takes a good chunk of the outside edge and rifles behind to the deep third fence. A famous, famous win for the Men in Blue as they made chasing 199 look like a stroll in the park.
 15:37 (IST) Oct 27 India aren't quite there yet as they lose another wicket. Naman Dhir is the new batter in.
 15:36 (IST) Oct 27 India vs New Zealand Live Score : 195/4 (13.1 overs) W Overs 13.1 Score 195 - 4 Kyle Jamieson to Sanju Samson, OUT! YOU MISS, I HIT! Some late joy for New Zealand before they head to Auckland. Kyle cannons in a very full ball, aimed at the stumps. Sanju Samson exposes the sticks by backing away and looking to loft it over the off side. But he gets a tad late to bring his bat down and misses to connect as the ball makes an absolute mess of the timber behind. India are 195/4, needing 4 more.

Duffy overruns and slips a bit while trying to stop the ball and it gets deflected away for a single.
 15:33 (IST) Oct 27 The next batter is Tilak Varma.
 15:32 (IST) Oct 27 India vs New Zealand Live Score : 193/3 (12.4 overs) W Overs 12.4 Score 193 - 3 Mitchell Santner to Shreyas Iyer, OUT! CAUGHT! Santner, who is yet to concede a boundary, picks up a wicket. He dishes out a full toss that drifts into the batter. Iyer sinks his back knee into the pitch and tries to slog it over deep mid-wicket, but his bat gets twisted at the point of contact while dragging it across. Hence, his timing goes all wrong and he offers a straightforward catch to deep mid-wicket. Phillips is not dropping those at all. India are 193/3, needing 6 more to win.

Samson waits back before lifting it inside-out to deep cover for a run more.

Shreyas Iyer is nearly beaten in the flight as he looks to drive, but adjusts and cuts it late to the left of short third for a couple of runs.

Sanju Samson stays leg side of the ball and squeezes it away to the right of the diving point fielder for a single.
 15:19 (IST) Oct 27 DRINKS! Time for a breather as Abhishek Sharma walks back to rousing applause from the crowd, and he gives a hug to the incoming Shreyas Iyer on his way back to the dugout. Right then, in terms of this contest, India need just 21 more off 60 balls and have a series win in their sights. Shouldn't be much of a fuss, but the Kiwis will look to delay the inevitable for as long as possible. The Indian skipper, Shreyas Iyer, is the new batter in.
 15:18 (IST) Oct 27 India vs New Zealand Live Score : 178/2 (9.6 overs) Score after 10 overs 178 - 2 Runs Scored: 0 1 1 4 6 4 0(W) Abhishek Sharma 113 (38) 
 Sanju Samson 8 (5) 
 Kyle Jamieson 2 - 0 - 36 - 1 W Overs 9.6 Score 178 - 2 Kyle Jamieson to Abhishek Sharma, OUT! IN THE AIR AND CAUGHT! This time, GP makes no mistake with a comparatively simple catch. The crowd rises up to applaud a tremendous knock from Abhishek. India are 178/2. Full and outside off, Abhishek advances but fails to get to the pitch of it. He tries to heave it across the line, the bat turning slightly in his hands as he connects off the inside half towards deep mid-wicket. Glenn Phillips settles under it and takes a safe catch.
 15:17 (IST) Oct 27 India vs New Zealand Live Score : 178/1 (9.5 overs) 4 Overs 9.5 Score 178 - 1 Kyle Jamieson to Abhishek Sharma, DROPPED AND FOUR! A Superman effort by Phillips. Full marks for the effort. Short of a length on leg stump and angled across the left-hander. Abhishek backs away and pulls it to the left of deep mid-wicket but gets it a bit mistimed off the inner half of the bat. Glenn Phillips launches himself full stretch to his left, almost like a Superman, but cannot hold on. He gets fingertips to it, but it deflects and lands just short of the rope. The umpires check the replay before signalling four. Only Phillips could have got anywhere near that one.
 15:17 (IST) Oct 27 India vs New Zealand Live Score : 174/1 (9.4 overs) 6 Overs 9.4 Score 174 - 1 Kyle Jamieson to Abhishek Sharma, SIX! In a hurry to finish things off now! A juicy half-volley, on the stumps, Abhishek swings it effortlessly over deep square leg. Targets the smallest boundary and clears it with ease.
 15:15 (IST) Oct 27 India vs New Zealand Live Score : 168/1 (9.3 overs) 4 Overs 9.3 Score 168 - 1 Kyle Jamieson to Abhishek Sharma, FOUR! Top edge, but that won't matter. HUNDRED FOR ABHISHEK SHARMA! Off just 35 balls, graced with ten sixes and four boundaries. That's his 4th T20I century. Astonishing batting from him as he has set Wellington on fire. Seems to be an off-pace delivery, on a good length, Abhishek Sharma is early into the pull shot and top edges it over the short fine leg for a boundary to get to his milestone. After all that mayhem, he folds himself into a yoga pose, perfectly calm, before breaking out an Erling Haaland-style celebration. The crowd is on its feet, roaring in appreciation of a truly special knock. They have surely got their money's worth.

He plays off the back foot and tucks it through mid-wicket for a single. The crowd is boisterous as Abhishek is on strike now.

 Matthew Fisher 1 - 0 - 23 - 1 4 Overs 7.6 Score 156 - 1 Matthew Fisher to Sanju Samson, FOUR! That is such a sweetly timed shot! Slightly back of a length and around the off stump, Sanju makes room by backing away and thumps it over the mid off fielder for a cracking boundary. Excellent backlift and balance on that shot. Absolutely no respite for the bowlers here in Wellington. Despite a wicket, 23 runs come off Fisher's first over.
